subject: science
prompt_en: What colour does blue litmus turn in an acid, and what colour does red litmus turn in a base?
prompt_hi: Neela litmus acid mein kis rang ka ho jaata hai, aur laal litmus base mein kis rang ka?
answer: Blue litmus turns red in an acid; red litmus turns blue in a base.

subject: science
prompt_en: Mix a pinch of haldi in a little water and wipe it on a strip of white paper to make it yellow. Predict: what will happen when you touch it with soap water? And with lemon juice?
prompt_hi: Thodi haldi paani mein milaao aur safed kaagaz ki patti pe laga ke use peela kar do. Guess karo: is pe sabun ka paani lagaoge toh kya hoga? Aur nimbu ka ras lagaoge toh?
answer: With soap water it turns red (reddish-brown) because soap is basic; with lemon juice it stays yellow, because turmeric does not change colour in an acid.

subject: science
prompt_en: Soak a few red hibiscus (gudhal) petals in warm water until the water turns coloured. Predict the colour when you add a few drops of it to (a) lemon juice and (b) baking soda solution.
prompt_hi: Laal gudhal ke kuch petals garam paani mein bhigo do jab tak paani rangeen na ho jaaye. Guess karo, iski kuch boondein (a) nimbu ke ras mein aur (b) baking soda ke ghol mein daalne pe kya rang aayega?
answer: (a) In lemon juice it turns dark pink or magenta because lemon juice is acidic. (b) In baking soda solution it turns green because baking soda solution is basic.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: will sugar solution change the colour of turmeric paper, blue litmus or red litmus? What does your prediction tell you about sugar solution?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: kya cheeni ka ghol haldi wale kaagaz, neele litmus ya laal litmus ka rang badlega? Isse cheeni ke ghol ke baare mein kya pata chalta hai?
answer: None of them changes colour, because sugar solution is neutral: neither acidic nor basic.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why do scientists use indicators instead of tasting substances to find out whether they are acids or bases?
prompt_hi: Scientists acid ya base pata karne ke liye chakhne ki bajaye indicators kyon use karte hain?
answer: Tasting or touching unknown substances can be dangerous because strong acids and bases burn and some substances are poisonous; indicators show the type safely through a colour change.

subject: science
prompt_en: Two clear liquids, A and B. Liquid A turns blue litmus red. Liquid B turns red litmus blue. Which could be vinegar and which could be soap solution? Why?
prompt_hi: Do saaf liquid hain, A aur B. A neele litmus ko laal karta hai. B laal litmus ko neela karta hai. Inmein se kaun sirka ho sakta hai aur kaun sabun ka paani? Kyon?
answer: A could be vinegar, because acids turn blue litmus red; B could be soap solution, because bases turn red litmus blue.

subject: science
prompt_en: Kabir writes in his notebook: 'Lime water turned red litmus blue, so lime water is an acid.' Find the mistake.
prompt_hi: Kabir apni copy mein likhta hai: 'Choone ke paani ne laal litmus ko neela kar diya, isliye choone ka paani acid hai.' Galti dhoondo.
answer: Turning red litmus blue shows a base, not an acid; lime water is basic.

subject: science
prompt_en: Make a three-column table with the headings acidic, basic and neutral. Place these by their indicator results: lemon juice, soap solution, sugar water, baking soda solution, vinegar, salt water. Say how you decided each one.
prompt_hi: 3 column wali table banao: acidic, basic aur neutral. Inhe indicator ke result ke hisaab se rakho: nimbu ka ras, sabun ka paani, cheeni ka paani, baking soda ka ghol, sirka, namak ka paani. Har ek ke liye batao kaise decide kiya.
answer: Acidic: lemon juice and vinegar (turn blue litmus red, hibiscus pink). Basic: soap solution and baking soda solution (turn red litmus blue, turmeric red, hibiscus green). Neutral: sugar water and salt water (no indicator changes).

subject: science
prompt_en: Your aunt's red cabbage sabzi turned bluish-green when a pinch of baking soda (khane ka soda) went into it. What does this tell you about red cabbage?
prompt_hi: Tumhari chachi ki laal patta gobhi ki sabzi mein chutki bhar khane ka soda gaya aur wo neeli-hari ho gayi. Isse laal patta gobhi ke baare mein kya pata chalta hai?
answer: Red cabbage contains a natural indicator: it changes to blue-green or green in a base such as baking soda (and turns pinkish-red in an acid).

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to your younger sister how she could find out, without tasting, whether a mystery clear liquid is acidic, basic or neutral, using only haldi paper and gudhal water.
prompt_hi: Apni chhoti behen ko samjhao ki bina chakhe, sirf haldi wale kaagaz aur gudhal ke paani se, wo kaise pata kar sakti hai ki ek anjaan saaf liquid acidic hai, basic hai ya neutral.
answer: Put a drop on haldi paper: if it turns red, the liquid is basic. If it stays yellow, it is acidic or neutral, so test with gudhal water: dark pink means acidic, no change from its own colour means neutral, and green would mean basic.

subject: science
prompt_en: Quick recall from last time: which indicator turns red in soap solution, and which indicator turns red in lemon juice?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se jaldi batao: kaunsa indicator sabun ke paani mein laal hota hai, aur kaunsa nimbu ke ras mein laal hota hai?
answer: Turmeric turns red in soap solution (a base); blue litmus turns red in lemon juice (an acid).

subject: science
prompt_en: Drain-cleaning powder contains caustic soda, which is a base. Why does its packet warn you to wear gloves, if bases are the 'opposite' of acids?
prompt_hi: Naali saaf karne wale powder mein caustic soda hota hai, jo ek base hai. Agar base acid ka 'ulta' hai, toh iske packet pe gloves pehenne ki warning kyon hoti hai?
answer: Strong bases are corrosive too and can burn skin and eyes, just like strong acids; 'opposite' in chemistry does not mean 'safe'.

subject: science
prompt_en: What two things are formed when an acid neutralises a base? What else is given out?
prompt_hi: Jab acid aur base ka neutralisation hota hai toh kaunsi do cheezein banti hain? Aur kya nikalta hai?
answer: A salt and water are formed, and heat is given out.

subject: science
prompt_en: Add a few drops of hibiscus water to some lemon juice: it turns pink. Now add baking soda solution little by little, stirring. Predict what you will see happen.
prompt_hi: Thode nimbu ke ras mein gudhal ke paani ki kuch boondein daalo: wo gulaabi ho jaata hai. Ab dheere dheere baking soda ka ghol daalte aur hilaate jao. Guess karo kya hota dikhega?
answer: It fizzes with bubbles of carbon dioxide; the pink slowly fades as the acid is neutralised, and when extra baking soda is added it turns green because the mixture has become basic.

subject: science
prompt_en: An ant bite stings because the ant injects formic acid. Predict whether rubbing on (a) lemon juice or (b) a paste of baking soda would give relief, and why.
prompt_hi: Cheenti ke kaatne pe jalan isliye hoti hai kyonki cheenti formic acid daalti hai. Guess karo, (a) nimbu ka ras ya (b) baking soda ka paste lagaane se aaraam milega, aur kyon?
answer: The baking soda paste, because it is a base and neutralises the acid; lemon juice is itself an acid and would not neutralise it.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why might a doctor suggest an antacid such as milk of magnesia when someone has acidity, a burning feeling after a heavy, spicy meal?
prompt_hi: Bhaari, teekha khaana khaane ke baad kisi ko acidity, yaani jalan, ho toh doctor milk of magnesia jaisa antacid kyon dete hain?
answer: The stomach makes hydrochloric acid to digest food; too much of it causes the burning. An antacid is a mild base that neutralises the extra acid.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare: Glass A has lemon juice with a lot of water added. Glass B has lemon juice with just the right amount of baking soda added. Which one has been neutralised? How would hibiscus water tell you?
prompt_hi: Tulna karo: Glass A mein nimbu ke ras mein bahut paani daala gaya. Glass B mein nimbu ke ras mein bilkul sahi maatra mein baking soda daala gaya. Kiska neutralisation hua? Gudhal ka paani ye kaise bataayega?
answer: Glass B is neutralised; glass A is only diluted and still acidic. Hibiscus water turns pink in A but shows no pink in B.

subject: science
prompt_en: A farmer's soil test shows that his soil is too acidic for his crop. What could he add to it, and why?
prompt_hi: Ek kisaan ki mitti ki jaanch se pata chalta hai ki mitti fasal ke liye bahut acidic hai. Wo usme kya mila sakta hai, aur kyon?
answer: Quicklime or slaked lime (chuna), which is a base, to neutralise the acid in the soil.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why does brushing your teeth after eating sweets help protect them? Use the idea of acids and bases.
prompt_hi: Meetha khaane ke baad brush karne se daant kyon bachte hain? Acid aur base ka idea use karke samjhao.
answer: Bacteria in the mouth break down sugary food left on the teeth and make acids that damage the tooth enamel. Toothpaste is basic and neutralises these acids, and brushing removes the leftover food.

subject: science
prompt_en: Anu says, 'Never mix an acid with a base; it always makes poison.' What would you tell Anu?
prompt_hi: Anu kehti hai, 'Acid ko kabhi base ke saath mat milao, isse hamesha zeher banta hai.' Tum Anu ko kya bataoge?
answer: Neutralisation usually gives a salt and water, which are often harmless, for example common salt and water; we use it safely in antacids and for ant bites. Strong acids and bases are dangerous to handle themselves.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw a colour strip of four boxes showing hibiscus water in: lemon juice alone, lemon juice with a little baking soda, lemon juice with just enough baking soda, and lemon juice with too much baking soda. Label each box acidic, neutral or basic.
prompt_hi: Chaar box wali ek colour strip banao jo dikhaye gudhal ka paani: sirf nimbu ke ras mein, thode baking soda ke saath, bilkul sahi maatra ke saath, aur bahut zyada baking soda ke saath. Har box pe acidic, neutral ya basic likho.
answer: Box 1: dark pink, acidic. Box 2: lighter pink, still acidic. Box 3: the extract's own purplish colour with no pink, neutral. Box 4: green, basic.

subject: science
prompt_en: Factories must treat acidic waste water with a base before letting it flow into a river. Why?
prompt_hi: Factories ko acidic gande paani ko nadi mein chhodne se pehle base se treat karna padta hai. Kyon?
answer: Acidic water would harm fish, water plants and the people and animals who use the river; neutralising it with a base makes it much safer before release.

subject: science
prompt_en: Teach your friend what neutralisation is, with one example from home and one from a farm.
prompt_hi: Apne dost ko sikhao ki neutralisation kya hota hai, ek example ghar se aur ek khet se.
answer: Neutralisation is when an acid and a base cancel each other's effect, forming salt and water and giving out heat. Home: baking soda on an ant bite or an antacid for acidity. Farm: adding lime to acidic soil.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: why is baking soda rubbed on an ant bite?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: cheenti ke kaatne pe baking soda kyon lagaate hain?
answer: The ant injects formic acid; baking soda is a base that neutralises it.

subject: science
prompt_en: You have one cell, one torch bulb and two wires. Describe how to connect them so that the bulb glows.
prompt_hi: Tumhare paas ek cell, ek torch bulb aur do taar hain. Batao inhe kaise jodoge ki bulb jal jaaye.
answer: Join one wire from the + terminal to one terminal of the bulb (for example its metal side), and the other wire from the bulb's other terminal (the tip at its base) to the − terminal, making one complete loop.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict before you try: a wire joins the cell's + terminal to the bulb's base tip, but the cell's − terminal is not joined to anything. Will the bulb glow?
prompt_hi: Try karne se pehle guess karo: ek taar cell ke + terminal ko bulb ke neeche ke tip se jodta hai, par cell ka − terminal kisi se nahi juda. Kya bulb jalega?
answer: No. The path is not complete; current needs a closed loop that goes back to the other terminal of the cell.

subject: science
prompt_en: Two identical bulbs are joined one after the other in a single loop with a cell. Predict: will the second bulb, the one the current reaches 'later', be dimmer than the first?
prompt_hi: Do bilkul ek jaise bulb ek hi loop mein ek ke baad ek cell ke saath jode gaye. Guess karo: kya doosra bulb, jahaan current 'baad mein' pahunchta hai, pehle se kam jalega?
answer: No, both glow equally brightly, because the same current flows through both; current is not used up along the loop. (Both are dimmer than one bulb alone would be.)

subject: science
prompt_en: A torch needs two cells. Predict: will it light if one cell is put in the wrong way round, so that both + ends face each other?
prompt_hi: Ek torch mein do cell lagte hain. Guess karo: agar ek cell ulta lag jaaye, yaani dono + sire aamne-saamne hon, toh kya torch jalegi?
answer: No (or only very faintly): the two cells push current in opposite directions and cancel each other. Cells must be joined + to −.

subject: science
prompt_en: A torch bulb looks fine from outside but does not glow, even with new cells. Why might that be?
prompt_hi: Torch ka bulb bahar se theek dikhta hai par naye cell daalne pe bhi nahi jalta. Aisa kyon ho sakta hai?
answer: Its filament may be broken (the bulb has fused), so the path through the bulb is broken and the circuit is open; or a contact may be loose.

subject: science
prompt_en: Arjun says current comes out of both ends of the cell and crashes together in the bulb to make light. Meera says current flows one way round the whole loop. Who is right, and what could show it?
prompt_hi: Arjun kehta hai current cell ke dono siron se nikal ke bulb mein takraata hai aur roshni banti hai. Meera kehti hai current poore loop mein ek hi disha mein behta hai. Kaun sahi hai, aur ye kaise dikha sakte hain?
answer: Meera is right. An LED lights only when it is joined one particular way round, which shows current has one direction; the same current flows all around the loop.

subject: science
prompt_en: Inside a torch there are no loose wires. What parts complete the circuit instead?
prompt_hi: Torch ke andar khule taar nahi hote. Unki jagah circuit ko kaun poora karta hai?
answer: Metal strips, the spring and the metal body or case, along with the switch, connect the cells' terminals to the bulb, forming a closed loop when the switch is on.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why is it safe to do circuit experiments with torch cells but never with the plug socket at home?
prompt_hi: Torch ke cell se circuit experiment karna safe kyon hai, par ghar ke plug socket se kabhi nahi?
answer: A cell gives a small voltage (about 1.5 V) that cannot push dangerous current through our body; the mains is about 230 V and can push enough current through the body to cause a severe shock or death.

subject: science
prompt_en: Riddhi's worksheet says: 'The bulb glows because electricity comes from the bulb and goes into the cell.' Spot the mistake.
prompt_hi: Riddhi ki worksheet mein likha hai: 'Bulb isliye jalta hai kyonki bijli bulb se nikal ke cell mein jaati hai.' Galti pakdo.
answer: The cell is the source: it pushes current around the circuit through the bulb. The bulb does not make electricity; it changes electrical energy into light and heat.

subject: science
prompt_en: Look at four set-ups: (A) one wire from + to the bulb's tip; (B) both wires from the cell touching only the bulb's tip; (C) one wire from + to the bulb's side, another from the bulb's tip to −; (D) both wires from the same + terminal to the bulb. In which does the bulb glow? Explain what is wrong with the others.
prompt_hi: Chaar set-up dekho: (A) sirf ek taar + se bulb ke tip tak; (B) cell ke dono taar sirf bulb ke tip ko chhoote hain; (C) ek taar + se bulb ki side tak, doosra bulb ke tip se − tak; (D) dono taar ek hi + terminal se bulb tak. Kismein bulb jalega? Baaki mein kya galat hai, batao.
answer: Only C. A: the loop is not complete. B: both wires touch one bulb terminal, so current does not pass through the filament. D: both wires come from the same cell terminal, so there is no loop through the cell.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to your younger brother why the bulb glows only when the loop is complete, and why the bulb does not 'eat up' the electricity.
prompt_hi: Apne chhote bhai ko samjhao ki bulb tabhi kyon jalta hai jab loop poora ho, aur bulb bijli ko 'kha' kyon nahi jaata.
answer: Current can flow only around a complete loop from one terminal of the cell, through the bulb, back to the other; a gap anywhere stops it everywhere. The same current comes out of the bulb as goes in; what gets used up is the cell's stored energy, which the bulb turns into light and heat.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: what is a closed circuit?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: closed circuit kya hota hai?
answer: A complete, unbroken path from one terminal of the cell, through the device, back to the other terminal, so current can flow.

subject: science
prompt_en: How is an open switch drawn differently from a closed switch in a circuit diagram?
prompt_hi: Circuit diagram mein khula (open) switch band (closed) switch se alag kaise banaya jaata hai?
answer: An open switch is drawn with a gap in the line (the lever not touching across); a closed switch is drawn with the gap bridged so the line is continuous.

subject: science
prompt_en: A circuit has a cell, a bulb and a switch that is OFF. Predict: if we take the switch out completely and join the two wires directly, will the bulb glow?
prompt_hi: Ek circuit mein cell, bulb aur OFF switch hai. Guess karo: agar switch poora nikaal ke dono taar seedhe jod dein, toh kya bulb jalega?
answer: Yes. The switch does not make electricity; joining the wires completes the loop just as an ON switch does.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: in a single loop, if the switch is moved from before the bulb to after the bulb, will it still turn the bulb on and off?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: ek single loop mein agar switch ko bulb se pehle wali jagah se hata ke bulb ke baad laga dein, toh kya wo phir bhi bulb ko on-off karega?
answer: Yes. A break anywhere in a single loop stops the current everywhere in it.

subject: science
prompt_en: A circuit diagram shows a battery of two cells joined + to −, a bulb and a closed switch. If the battery is replaced by just one cell, predict what changes.
prompt_hi: Ek circuit diagram mein do cell ki battery (+ se −), ek bulb aur band switch hai. Agar battery ki jagah sirf ek cell laga dein, toh guess karo kya badlega?
answer: The bulb still glows, but more dimly, because one cell pushes a smaller current than two.
